title: Best time to SELL is 2026-2027 (this is what a 100 year old prediction says. Let's Analyze.
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
summary: Akshat Shrivastava uses Samuel Benner's chart - which flagged 1999, 2007, 2016 and 2026 as years to sell assets, ahead of the dot-com crash, the financial crisis and a US-China trade-war period, and 2023 as a panic year - to ask whether 2026-2027 is the time to sell, then grounds the answer in macro data rather than the prediction itself. He argues inflation is structural and understated by headline CPI: memory prices are up about 80% in a year, older iPhones about 9%, and AI subscriptions such as Claude about 60-70%, pushing up hardware, software and data-centre costs. The US, he says, is pushing growth by funnelling debt into AI, has secured its energy needs, and benefits from exporting inflation and debasing its roughly $40 trillion debt. India, by contrast, is in survival mode - no AI growth engine, not energy-secure, and facing both a growth and an inflation problem - with parallels to the 1970s: oil shock, loose money and gold restrictions. For portfolios he advises diversification above all: keep 20-30% liquid in short- or medium-duration bonds and for writing puts, avoid long-dated treasuries, add gold on falls, hold land and villas, and favour US equities (illustratively 60% QQQ / 40% S&P 500), with equities at 50-60% overall and India at 30-40% of the equity portion, or a 50/50 India-US split. No individual Indian stock call with a stated ₹ price is made. Captions are clean, though several chart figures are described verbally rather than shown as text.
